plan.name: plan
plan.textSnippet: Every program so far has used somebody else’s songs. This one is yours: five real songs you choose, and a program that does five different things to them. One of the jobs uses Python nobody has shown
plan.contentAnchor: Every program so far has used somebody else’s songs. This one is yours: five real songs you choose, and a program that does five different things to them. One of the jobs uses Python nobody has shown you yet, so here it is. import random, on the very first line, switches on Python's picking tools. random.choice(playlist) then picks one title from the list at random — it can be a different one every run. There are no ready-made lines to drag across on this card: you type the program yourself. At the top of the card are the five jobs your engine has to do. Every time you press RUN, each job says done as soon as your program really does that job.

bench.name: bench
bench.textSnippet: Not sure where to start? Press the button below. It writes the whole shape into the box where you type your program, and leaves every song title blank for you to fill in.
bench.contentAnchor: Not sure where to start? Press the button below. It writes the whole shape into the box where you type your program, and leaves every song title blank for you to fill in.
bench.cardText: Write a playlist engine that does five things to five songs of your own. · THE FIVE JOBS YOUR ENGINE HAS TO DO · 1NOT CHECKED YET · It ADDS a song, so the list ends up longer than the one you typed. · 2NOT CHECKED YET · It TAKES ONE OUT, so one of your songs is gone by the end. · 3NOT CHECKED YET · It picks a song AT RANDOM and prints a line about it. · 4NOT CHECKED YET · The list ends up in A to Z order. · 5NOT CHECKED YET · It prints a Now Playing heading and then exactly THREE of your songs.
bench.says: the BENCH face: the five jobs along the top, the empty typing box with its line numbers, and the free help row
